Prophecy as to an Attack on Jerusalem.</title> <div sID="gen14361" type="x-p"/> That by Sennacherib, in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah; <reference osisRef="Isa.22.8-Isa.22.11">Is 22:8-11</reference>, the preparations for defense and securing of water exactly answer to those in <reference osisRef="2Chr.32.4">2Ch 32:4</reference>, 5, 30. "Shebna," too (<reference osisRef="Isa.22.15">Is 22:15</reference>), was scribe at this time (<reference osisRef="Isa.36.3">Is 36:3</reference>) [Maurer]. The language of <reference osisRef="Isa.22.12-Isa.22.14">Is 22:12-14</reference>, as to the infidelity and consequent utter ruin of the Jews, seems rather to foreshadow the destruction by Nebuchadnezzar in Zedekiah's reign, and cannot be restricted to Hezekiah's time [Lowth].<div eID="gen14361" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14362" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8693"/><hi type="bold">1. of ... valley of vision--</hi>rather, "respecting the valley of visions"; namely, Jerusalem, the seat of divine revelations and visions, "the nursery of prophets" [Jerome], (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.3">Is 2:3</reference>; 29:1; <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.4">Eze 23:4</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="Luke.13.33">Lu 13:33</reference>). It lay in a "valley" surrounded by hills higher than Zion and Moriah (<reference osisRef="Ps.125.2">Psa 125:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.21.13">Jr 21:13</reference>).<div eID="gen14362" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14363" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thee--</hi>the people of Jerusalem personified.<div eID="gen14363" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14364" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">housetops--</hi>Panic-struck, they went up on the flat balustraded roofs to look forth and see whether the enemy was near, and partly to defend themselves from the roofs (<reference osisRef="Judg.9.51">Jud 9:51</reference>, &c.). <div eID="gen14364" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 22 Is 22:1-14 . Prophecy as to an Attack on Jerusalem. That by Sennacherib, in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah; Is 22:8-11 , the preparations for defense and securing of water exactly answer to those in 2Ch 32:4 , 5, 30. "Shebna," too ( Is 22:15 ), was scribe at this time ( Is 36:3 ) [Maurer]. The language of Is 22:12-14 , as to the infidelity and consequent utter ruin of the Jews, seems rather to foreshadow the destruction by Nebuchadnezzar in Zedekiah's reign, and cannot be restricted to Hezekiah's time [Lowth]. 1. of ... valley of vision-- rather, "respecting the valley of visions"; namely, Jerusalem, the seat of divine revelations and visions, "the nursery of prophets" [Jerome], ( Is 2:3 ; 29:1; Eze 23:4 , Margin; Lu 13:33 ). It lay in a "valley" surrounded by hills higher than Zion and Moriah ( Psa 125:2 ; Jr 21:13 ). thee-- the people of Jerusalem personified. housetops-- Panic-struck, they went up on the flat balustraded roofs to look forth and see whether the enemy was near, and partly to defend themselves from the roofs ( Jud 9:51 , &c.).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8694"/><div sID="gen14365" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8694"/><hi type="bold">2. art--</hi>rather, "wert"; for it could not now be said to be "a joyous city" (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.13">Is 32:13</reference>). The cause of their joy (<reference osisRef="Isa.22.13">Is 22:13</reference>) may have been because Sennacherib had accepted Hezekiah's offer to renew the payment of tribute, and they were glad to have peace on any terms, however humiliating (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.18.14-2Kgs.18.16">2Ki 18:14-16</reference>), or on account of the alliance with Egypt. If the reference be to Zedekiah's time, the joy and feasting are not inapplicable, for this recklessness was a general characteristic of the unbelieving Jews (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.12">Is 56:12</reference>).<div eID="gen14365" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14366" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not slain with the sword--</hi>but with the famine and pestilence about to be caused by the coming siege (<reference osisRef="Lam.4.9">La 4:9</reference>). Maurer refers this to the plague by which he thinks Sennacherib's army was destroyed, and Hezekiah was made sick (<reference osisRef="Isa.37.36">Is 37:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.38.1">38:1</reference>). But there is no authority for supposing that the Jews in the city suffered such extremities of plague at this time, when God destroyed their foes. Barnes refers it to those slain in flight, not in open honorable "battle"; <reference osisRef="Isa.22.3">Is 22:3</reference> favors this. <div eID="gen14366" type="x-p"/>

Isaiah says (<reference osisRef="Isa.22.8-Isa.22.13">Is 22:8-13</reference>) his countrymen will look to their own strength to defend themselves, while others of them will drown their sorrows as to their country in feasting, but none will look to Jehovah. <div eID="gen14386" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8701"/><div sID="gen14387" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8701"/><hi type="bold">9. Ye have seen--</hi>rather, "Ye shall see."<div eID="gen14387" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14388" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">city of David--</hi>the upper city, on Zion, the south side of Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="2Sam.5.7">2Sa 5:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Sam.5.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.8.1">1Ki 8:1</reference>); surrounded by a wall of its own; but even in it there shall be "breaches." Hezekiah's preparations for defense accord with this (<reference osisRef="2Chr.32.5">2Ch 32:5</reference>).<div eID="gen14388" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14389" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye gathered--</hi>rather, "ye shall gather."<div eID="gen14389" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14390" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lower pool--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Isa.22.11">Is 22:11</reference>). Ye shall bring together into the city by subterranean passages cut in the rock of Zion, the fountain from which the lower pool (only mentioned here) is supplied. See on <reference osisRef="Isa.7.3">Is 7:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.20.20">2Ki 20:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.32.3-2Chr.32.5">2Ch 32:3-5</reference>, represent Hezekiah as having stopped the fountains to prevent the Assyrians getting water. But this is consistent with the passage here. The superfluous waters of the lower pool usually flowed into Hinnom valley, and so through that of Jehoshaphat to the brook Kedron. Hezekiah built a wall round it, stopped the outflowing of its waters to debar the foe from the use of them, and turned them into the city. <div eID="gen14390" type="x-p"/>

The superfluous waters of the lower pool usually flowed into Hinnom valley, and so through that of Jehoshaphat to the brook Kedron. Hezekiah built a wall round it, stopped the outflowing of its waters to debar the foe from the use of them, and turned them into the city.

navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 22 Is 22:1-14 . Prophecy as to an Attack on Jerusalem. That by Sennacherib, in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah; Is 22:8-11 , the preparations for defense and securing of water exactly answer to those in 2Ch 32:4 , 5, 30. "Shebna," too ( Is 22:15 ), was scribe at this time ( Is 36:3 ) [Maurer]. The language of Is 22:12-14 , as to the infidelity and consequent utter ruin of the Jews, seems rather to foreshadow the destruction by Nebuchadnezzar in Zedekiah's reign, and cannot be restricted to Hezekiah's time [Lowth].
